cells.tense: You are holding what you built all the way to its end right now.
cells.ask: Choose one thing you built and use it exactly as it is for a week — no adjusting. Feel it stay up without your hands on it.
cells.core:
You know how to carry a thing all the way to its end. Not the loudest worker and not a passenger either — you take what you started and you stay with it until it stands, and it stands because you kept your grip on it.

On a good day you finish inside your own hours. You stack the last piece and you stop, done with the whole thing, the work resting on itself now. No leaning past today to push the next one up before this one has settled. That steadiness is quiet and it's yours. This week, one evening, let what you finished simply exist — look at it, use it, ask nothing more of it. The balance costs you that evening of not reaching.
cells.sheetLine: You hold what you built until it stands on its own.
cells.verb: carrying built work to full completion
cells.place: in the load that gets held and carried day after day

cells.tense: You will be straining to hold up the next thing before it ever arrives.
cells.ask: Let one thing you made sit untouched for three days — no polishing, no improving. Write down the first feeling that shows up before you pick it back up.
cells.core:
You're bracing already for the next thing you'll have to hold. Somewhere out there is a version where the work is finally safe, finally done, and you're already standing in it — so you're pushing today's load off balance to make room for a weight that hasn't shown up. That pushing takes from you the very thing it was meant to protect.

On a good day you set a thing down because it's finished. You look at the work and stop, nothing to race toward, nothing new already loaded. That ease is what you're trading away. Feel one thing rest with nobody holding it and see that it stays up.

cells.tense: You stood at the end of the old cycle and did not take up the weight again.
cells.ask: Pick one small thing that fell by the side and carry it through to done today — not yesterday's big thing, just the closest one you left behind.
cells.core:
The ability to hold is still in you. It just isn't holding anything. At some point the load felt too heavy or the ending felt wrong, and you stopped mid-carry — and you didn't quite come back to your place in it. The stamina is there. The grip is with you. The load being carried isn't.

On a good day you pick something up because it's yours to carry and you hold it without having to prove anything by lifting. You shine that way, not to show it off. Today, choose one thing that fell by the side when the old cycle ended and carry it through to done. Not the biggest thing — the nearest.

cells.tense: You keep the finished work standing, then say it stands on its own.
cells.ask: Say once, to one person, "I built that" about a piece of the work you've been calling simply the job.
cells.core:
You keep the work standing — you steady it every week, you take the weight when it creaks — but you describe it as if it held itself. So the finishing keeps happening and your name stays off it. The hands stay under it. The claim on that does not.

On a good day you know the thing stands because you kept it up, and you shine that way without needing to announce it. That knowing shows in how you look at what's done. Today, say once, out loud to someone, "I built that" — about one piece you've been calling just the work.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it standing, then call it nobody's.
cells.verb: carrying built work to full completion
cells.place: in the load that gets held and carried day after day

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person's building has already reached its natural completion, or is bracing against lifting anything again. The record says only that directed agency is fully materialized through sustained effort, seated in holding capacity, at Balanced, in excess, in deficit, or unclaimed. A reader could reasonably say the structure is not finished and nothing has gone up yet — that the work is plain ongoing, not a legacy that already stands. The asks survive being wrong: each is one visible action done inside a shared day, needs no money or free time, and teaches the partner something about their own grip on what they have made regardless of whether the card's read is exact. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person: call it a legacy. Nothing here says someone else named it one.
